|   |   `-- Native UI events enter here; platform-independent terminal behavior stays here

|   |   |-- Compile-time runtime selection: GTK, embedded, browser, or none
|   |   `-- rt_app.performAction() delegates titles, clipboard/UI actions, and window operations
|   `-- App connects multiple sessions (src/App.zig)
|       |-- surfaces: ArrayList(*apprt.Surface); focused_surface identifies the active session
|       |-- font_grid_set: font.SharedGridSet; device: ?*renderer.Device
|       |   `-- Surfaces reference shared fonts and borrow the app-scoped graphics device
|       `-- tick() -> drainMailbox() -> surfaceMessage() -> Surface.handleMessage()
|           `-- Worker-originated surface messages return to the application thread
|
|-- [O] Surface.init() assembles one session (src/Surface.zig)
|   |-- io: termio.Termio; io_thread: termio.Thread; io_thr: std.Thread
|   |-- renderer: Renderer; renderer_thread: renderer.Thread; renderer_thr: std.Thread
|   |-- renderer_state: renderer.State
|   |   |-- terminal = &self.io.terminal -- shared reference, not another terminal model
|   |   `-- mutex protects referenced terminal state and shared presentation inputs
|   |-- mouse / keyboard / pressed_key / focused / visible / readonly
|   |   `-- Interaction state belongs to the session, independently of the child process
|   `-- config: DerivedConfig; size: renderer.Size; font_grid_key
|       `-- Derived configuration avoids retaining the caller's Config memory
|
|-- [C] User input -> bindings or terminal bytes (src/Surface.zig)
|   |-- keyCallback() first resolves configured keybindings and sequences
|   |   |-- Handled bindings perform actions rather than sending the key to the child
|   |   `-- encodeKey() -> input.key_encode.encode() for unconsumed input
|   |       `-- [D] KeyEvent + Options.fromTerminal() -> protocol-specific bytes
|   |           `-- Terminal modes and active-screen keyboard settings affect encoding
|   |-- Mouse / selection / paste paths
|   |   |-- input.mouse_encode: event + terminal reporting mode -> mouse protocol bytes
|   |   |-- Screen.select() retains a tracked selection for local interaction
|   |   `-- input.paste.encode(): paste contents + options -> terminal input sequences
|   `-- queueIo(.write_small / .write_stable / .write_alloc)
|       |-- readonly rejects writes while retaining local terminal interactions
|       `-- Termio.queueMessage() -> termio.Thread.drainMailbox() -> queueWrite()
|           `-- Exec.queueWrite() schedules bytes to the PTY (src/termio/Exec.zig)
|
|-- [C] Child output -> parsed terminal operations (src/termio/Termio.zig)
|   |-- backend: termio.Backend = .exec; Exec owns Subprocess
|   |   |-- Surface supplies command, environment, working directory, shell integration
|   |   `-- Exec.threadEnter() -> Subprocess.start(): create PTY and launch command
|   |       |-- Process watcher detects child exit
|   |       `-- ReadThread delivers output to Termio.processOutput()
|   |           |-- POSIX: io-gather batches PTY reads; io-reader parses batches
|   |           `-- Windows: one read loop reads and processes output
|   |-- processOutput() locks renderer_state.mutex
|   |   `-- processOutputLocked() -> terminal_stream.nextSlice(buf)
|   |       |-- terminal.Stream(StreamHandler) retains incremental parsing state
|   |       `-- StreamHandler.vt() / vtPrintAscii() dispatch terminal operations
|   |           `-- print, cursor movement, scrolling, modes, and attributes mutate Terminal
|   `-- StreamHandler bridges effects outside the grid (src/termio/stream_handler.zig)
|       |-- Terminal queries -> termio_mailbox -> reply bytes to the child
|       |-- Titles, bells, clipboard requests -> surface_mailbox -> runtime handling
|       `-- queueRender() / renderer_mailbox -> renderer wakeup and presentation updates
|
|-- [O] Termio.terminal is the authoritative emulator model (src/terminal/Terminal.zig)
|   |-- Exposes print(), cursor operations, resize(), scrollViewport(), and mode changes
|   |   `-- Renderer-agnostic state: no native window or GPU ownership
|   |-- screens: ScreenSet (src/terminal/ScreenSet.zig)
|   |   |-- primary screen exists initially; alternate screen initializes on demand
|   |   `-- active: *Screen chooses the current screen
|   |       |-- cursor / saved_cursor / selection / charset / kitty_keyboard
|   |       |-- kitty_images and semantic_prompt retain screen-specific protocol state
|   |       `-- pages: PageList (src/terminal/Screen.zig, src/terminal/PageList.zig)
|   |           |-- Ordered pages hold scrollback followed by the active screen
|   |           |-- Page rows/cells carry character and styling data
|   |           `-- Tracked pins keep cursor, viewport, and selection references meaningful
|   `-- rows / cols / scrolling_region / tabstops / modes / colors / title / pwd
|       `-- [D] Parsed output changes both visible contents and future input interpretation
|
|-- [C] Shared terminal state -> GPU presentation (src/renderer/Thread.zig)
|   |-- Wakeup -> drainMailbox() -> renderCallback() -> Renderer.updateFrame()
|   |-- Renderer = GenericRenderer(GraphicsAPI) (src/renderer.zig)
|   |   `-- GraphicsAPI is selected at compile time: Metal or OpenGL
|   |-- updateFrame() snapshots under State.lockDemand() / unlockDemand()
|   |   |-- terminal_state: terminal.RenderState retains renderer-side extracted state

|   |   |   `-- Combined with fonts, colors, sizing, mouse state, and IME preedit
|   |   `-- synchronized_output mode defers frame updates
|   |-- font_shaper / font_shaper_cache + font_grid -> glyph and cell rendering data
|   |   `-- src/renderer/generic.zig keeps frame construction separate from terminal parsing
|   `-- drawFrame() -> GraphicsAPI rendering and presentation
|       |-- Renderer scheduling considers visibility and vsync
|       `-- Surface.draw() can request synchronous drawing during native UI activity
|

|   |-- Surface.sizeCallback() -> resize() (src/Surface.zig)

|   |   `-- queueIo(.resize) and renderer mailbox carry the new size
|   |       `-- Termio.resize() (src/termio/Termio.zig)
|   |           |-- Under the terminal mutex: backend.resize() + Terminal.resize()
|   |           |   `-- Child redraw cannot be parsed against obsolete dimensions
|   |           `-- Notify renderer after emulator and PTY size changes
|   `-- App.updateConfig() -> Surface.handleMessage(.change_config)
|       `-- Surface, Termio, and Renderer maintain their own derived configuration

   501	/// Perform an app-wide binding action. If the action is surface-specific
   502	/// then it will be performed on all surfaces. To perform only app-scoped
   503	/// actions, use performAction.
   504	pub fn performAllAction(
   505	    self: *App,
   506	    rt_app: *apprt.App,
   507	    action: input.Binding.Action,
   508	) !void {
   509	    switch (action.scope()) {
   510	        // App-scoped actions are handled by the app so that they aren't
   511	        // repeated for each surface (since each surface forwards
   512	        // app-scoped actions back up).
   513	        .app => try self.performAction(
   514	            rt_app,
   515	            action.scoped(.app).?, // asserted through the scope match
   516	        ),
   517	
   518	        // Surface-scoped actions are performed on all surfaces. Errors
   519	        // are logged but processing continues.
   520	        .surface => for (self.surfaces.items) |surface| {
   521	            _ = surface.core().performBindingAction(action) catch |err| {
   522	                log.warn("error performing binding action on surface id={x} err={}", .{
   523	                    surface.core().id,
   524	                    err,
   525	                });
   526	            };
   527	        },
   528	    }
   529	}

    13	/// The mutex that must be held while reading any of the data in the
    14	/// members of this state. Note that the state itself is NOT protected
    15	/// by the mutex and is NOT thread-safe, only the members values of the
    16	/// state (i.e. the terminal, devmode, etc. values).
    17	mutex: *std.Io.Mutex,
    18	
    19	/// The terminal data.
    20	terminal: *terminalpkg.Terminal,
    21	
    22	/// The terminal inspector, if any. This will be null while the inspector
    23	/// is not active and will be set when it is active.
    24	inspector: ?*Inspector = null,
    25	
    26	/// Dead key state. This will render the current dead key preedit text
    27	/// over the cursor. This currently only ever renders a single codepoint.
    28	/// Preedit can in theory be multiple codepoints long but that is left as
    29	/// a future exercise.
    30	preedit: ?Preedit = null,
    31	
    32	/// Mouse state. This only contains state relevant to what renderers
    33	/// need about the mouse.
    34	mouse: Mouse = .{},
    35	
    36	/// The number of threads currently waiting to acquire `mutex` via
    37	/// `lockDemand`. This is not protected by the mutex; it is read by
    38	/// hot lock/unlock loops (the IO parse thread) in `yieldToDemand` to
    39	/// decide whether to hand the mutex off before relocking it.
    40	demand: std.atomic.Value(u32) = .init(0),
    41	
    42	/// Handoff generation counter. Incremented (with a futex wake) by
    43	/// `unlockDemand` after a demanding waiter releases the mutex, so that
    44	/// `yieldToDemand` knows the waiter had its turn.
    45	handoff_gen: std.atomic.Value(u32) = .init(0),
    46	
    47	/// How long `yieldToDemand` sleeps waiting for a demanding waiter to
    48	/// take its turn before giving up. This bounds how long the IO parse
    49	/// thread can stall if a wake is lost or the waiter is descheduled; a
    50	/// demanding critical section (the renderer's frame snapshot) is
    51	/// microseconds, so one millisecond is generous.
    52	const handoff_timeout_ns = 1 * std.time.ns_per_ms;
    53	
    54	/// Acquire `mutex` while signaling demand for it. Use this instead of
    55	/// locking the mutex directly on threads that must not be starved by
    56	/// a hot lock/unlock loop (the renderer's frame snapshot). Must be
    57	/// released with `unlockDemand`; releasing with `mutex.unlock` keeps
    58	/// the data safe but makes parked `yieldToDemand` callers wait out
    59	/// their full timeout.
    60	///
    61	/// Both `std.Thread.Mutex` and os_unfair_lock are unfair: a running
    62	/// thread that unlocks and immediately relocks beats a sleeping
    63	/// waiter every time, because the waiter must first be woken and
    64	/// scheduled. Under sustained pty output the IO parse thread is
    65	/// exactly such a loop, so without this signal the renderer can
    66	/// starve for as long as the output lasts.
    67	pub fn lockDemand(self: *State, io: std.Io) void {
    68	    _ = self.demand.fetchAdd(1, .monotonic);
    69	    self.mutex.lockUncancelable(io);
    70	    const prev = self.demand.fetchSub(1, .monotonic);
    71	    assert(prev > 0);
    72	}
    73	
    74	/// Release `mutex` acquired via `lockDemand` and notify hot loops
    75	/// parked in `yieldToDemand` that the demanding waiter had its turn.
    76	pub fn unlockDemand(self: *State, io: std.Io) void {
    77	    self.mutex.unlock(io);
    78	    _ = self.handoff_gen.fetchAdd(1, .monotonic);
    79	    io.futexWake(u32, &self.handoff_gen.raw, 1);
    80	}
    81	
    82	/// Called by hot lock/unlock loops between critical sections, with
    83	/// `mutex` NOT held: if a `lockDemand` waiter exists, sleep until it
    84	/// has acquired and released the mutex (or the timeout passes). This
    85	/// is the handoff that unfair mutexes never do on their own.
    86	///
    87	/// The orderings here are all monotonic because these atomics are a
    88	/// scheduling heuristic, not a synchronization boundary: the mutex
    89	/// itself orders the protected data, and the timeout bounds any
    90	/// staleness.
    91	pub fn yieldToDemand(self: *State, io: std.Io) void {
    92	    if (self.demand.load(.monotonic) == 0) return;
    93	
    94	    // Snapshot the generation before rechecking demand: if the waiter
    95	    // acquires and releases between our check and the wait below, the
    96	    // generation no longer matches and timedWait returns immediately.
    97	    const gen = self.handoff_gen.load(.monotonic);
    98	    if (self.demand.load(.monotonic) == 0) return;
    99	    io.futexWaitTimeout(
   100	        u32,
   101	        &self.handoff_gen.raw,
   102	        gen,
   103	        .{ .duration = .{ .raw = .fromNanoseconds(handoff_timeout_ns), .clock = .awake } },
   104	    ) catch {};
   105	}
